items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I arrived in London with Lily the 6th of April and learned that the tour would be made with the Bruce Turner orchestra.

ctx.x: So Ron kept knocking on doors and speaking about me until he finally caught the ears of someone that could see his idea in bringing me there. I was so close to the country and many American musicians were going there and transportation from the U.S.A. costed me more than it would from France. Eventually, I was contacted by a booking agent named Jim Godbolt, and we got together on the loot which was bread no hell after all I had heard about the good/man that was paid in England. But I wanted to get my foot in…

I arrived in London with Lily the 6th of April and learned that the tour would be made with the Bruce Turner orchestra. I knew of Bruce but had never met him. He had the reputation of being one of England's greatest alto sax players, and as the tour continued, I found this to be true. But first I must say that Lily and I liked the looks of everything from the moment we landed at Heathrow airport. And we became more and more excited as we approached the great city of London. A kitchenette apartment had been…

That afternoon we had a rehearsal at the Six Bells in Chealsea, which is a district of London. The Six Bells was a very well known place by musicians and jazz fans and there I met Bruce and the boys, Ray Crance, trumpet, Pete Strange, trombone, Tony Baylis, bass, Ron Ruben, piano, and Doug Higgins, drums, Jack Higgins, not related to Doug, was in charge of the jazz department at the Harold Davison Agency, but Jim Godbolt was going to take care of the band during the tour.
